axes.model_access: Open-source model aggregation is its native form: the in-page list "Models 137" and Omni auto-routing were visible on the day (official copy: "Omni automatically picks the best AI model… You can also choose from any available open source models") — users pick open-source models directly, all hosted on HF's inference side.
axes.runtime: Web (huggingface.co/chat); the frontend is open source (the chat-ui repo, Apache-2.0, ★11,004 / pushed 2026-10-30 verified via GitHub API same day) — self-deployable (the runner-class tools like text-generation-webui are a separate local route). The hosted version generates on HF's side.
axes.local_files: On the hosted version, chat history lives on the account/browser side; on a self-deployed version data stays entirely on your own machine (the structural difference from hosted chat products).
axes.background: Chat returns instantly; no official statement verified for an async-task form. A new "ML Intern" entry (papers/training/spaces-oriented) was on the page on the day.
axes.tools: MCP tool integration in the open-source frontend is on record in the official README (tools exposed by MCP servers called via OpenAI function calling; trusted servers can be preconfigured via env, users can add their own in the UI with a health check; the preconfigured example includes Web Search (Exa)); the hosted version runs on the same codebase, its exact toggle form not verified item by item.
axes.context: Chats organized per conversation; hosted history lives on the account/browser side. No official statement verified for cross-session memory — the open-source frontend's data layer is entirely under the self-deployer's control, the structural difference from hosted chat products.
axes.permissions: HF account optional (usable without login, with reduced features); data terms are governed jointly by HF's privacy page and each chosen model's license, not verified item by item.
axes.fit: Fits: open-source models only, lining up 137 open entries under one account, referencing/self-deploying an open-source chat frontend. Not a fit: closed-source flagship models (GPT/Claude are not on the list), direct mainland access (not filed).

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The coding-oriented test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md) (the coding task suite does not apply to chat products).

**Suggested measurements** (three, all pointing at things the official readable pages do not give):

- **Omni auto-routing's selection logic and explainability** (the official copy only says "picks the best")
- **Hosted-version chat-data retention and training terms** (read the HF privacy page item by item)
- **Cost of wiring inference backends to a self-deployed chat-ui** (the official docs give the path; hands-on untested)
unknowns:

related: Also multi-model aggregation: Poe's pool includes closed APIs, HuggingChat's pool is open-source models only.
Also an open-source-model route: Ollama runs locally, HuggingChat is hosted (and its frontend can be self-deployed against a local backend).
Open models also have a vendor-run entry: DeepSeek's official entry goes deep on one vendor, HuggingChat lays many side by side.
